Seminar Title:

ADVANCED PROCESSING AND MACHINE LEARNING-ASSISTED TECHNO-FUNCTIONAL ENHANCEMENT OF HYACINTH BEAN (LABLAB PURPUREUS) PROTEIN

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Food Process Engineering

Speaker Name:

Gorde Pratik Madhukar ( Rollno : 523fp3003)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

CH-306

Date and Time:

14 Oct 2026 4:30 PM

Contact:

Sushil Kumar Singh

Abstract:

Hyacinth bean (Lablab purpureus) is a drought-tolerant, underutilized legume containing around 27% protein, yet its landraces remain poorly characterized, and no commercial protein ingredient is derived from it. This work combines machine learning, non-thermal processing and process equipment design to convert hyacinth bean into a functional protein ingredient. Twelve landrace accessions from western India were identified by FTIR spectroscopy and computer vision. Among 25 regression and 25 classification models, an optimized neural network gave R2=0.96, and an optimized k-nearest neighbor classifier reached 99.52% accuracy. EfficientNet classified seed images with an F1 score of 98.25%. A YOLOv5 model fitted with a texture enhancement block detected six seed quality classes with 96.8% accuracy and a mAP@50 of 92.3%. Engineering, proximate, phytochemical and mineral profiling, together with principal component and hierarchical cluster analysis, identified BAHB-9 as the superior accession. It contained 29.40% crude protein and 813.30 &mug/g iron and showed 66.42% DPPH scavenging. Protein from this accession was then extracted and modified by non-thermal techniques. Multipin cold plasma at 15 kV for 80 min increased the solubility of the alkaline-extracted isolate by about 21%, its water absorption capacity by 40% and its oil absorption capacity by 60%. Treatment at 20 kV for 100 min instead caused aggregation and loss of function. Ultrasound-assisted extraction at 70% amplitude for 20 min raised yield from 20.41% to 29.24% and purity from 71.42% to 81.23%. Among five extraction-modification routes, ultrasound-assisted extraction followed by cold plasma produced the greatest structural unfolding. This route raised solubility by 22.58%, oil absorption by 50.87% and emulsion stability by 126.08%. A manothermosonication reactor coupling ultrasound, temperature and pressure was designed and fabricated for protein extraction and modification. The modified hyacinth bean protein has potential application in development of high-moisture meat analogues.
